title: ECI affidavit to Court has unresolved questions, unbroken silences
shows: The Indian Express's editorial calls the Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 underwhelming and says it raises more questions than it answers. By the paper's account the affidavit treats the 14 objections Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu recorded in 10 months as part of the consultative process, while most of them were about orders already issued and decisions taken without the two being told. The editorial says the affidavit rolls back the changes made to Form 6 for first-time voters online and sets up a committee that includes experts to review whether ECINet complies with the law, without acknowledging the mistake or holding anyone accountable. It notes that 88 of the 97 Goa voters left off the final rolls have since applied through Form 6, and asks why the software blocked, in February, the registration officers' decisions to reverse the deletions. On West Bengal it says the affidavit names the office of the state's Chief Electoral Officer as the filer of appeals against orders restoring voters, and asks why the two Commissioners were kept in the dark when they asked about it earlier. It cites the paper's report that judges of the tribunals the Court appointed to decide SIR appeals in West Bengal say the Commission's requirement for Aadhaar authentication in its portal is in their way, and asks the Supreme Court to nudge the Commission towards a course correction that begins with fuller transparency.
quote: The affidavit is an imperfect start. The Court, which has a distinguished record of upholding Article 324 that secures the ECI’s powers, must now nudge it towards a course correction.
note: Online headline from the page, 'ECI affidavit to Court has unresolved questions, unbroken silences', published 28 October 2026 at 6:00 am IST by Editorial, with the full text served on the page. The print edition of the same day carries it as 'ECI affidavit to Court has unbroken silences', read from the printed page supplied by the owner, which has the same text. Every claim in the summary is the paper's. The affidavit is court-52 in disputes_research/courts.json. The Indian Express report of 27 October summarised there gives the same 88 of the 97 Goa electors as the affidavit's figure. The Commission's press note of 26 September (ECI/PN/120/2026, paragraph 3) gave 81 of 97. On Form 6, the affidavit as Bar and Bench reported it says Form 6 was not amended, since only the Central Government can amend it, accepts that the way the declaration was shown online could be read as an amendment, and records a decision of the ER Division of 21 October 2026 to split the online application into two parts as the paper forms are. The words 'rolls back' are the editorial's description of that decision. The affidavit itself was not read.
